coordinates.locator: OSM D0 Assembly Building centroid (extract of 2026-09-18)
coordinates.note: `kind: campus` under A23: the point is an OpenStreetMap building centroid (rank-11 source), which A17 does not admit as a detector-grade point on its own; it is nevertheless within ~40 m of the hall. The D0 assembly/collision hall building is mapped in OpenStreetMap; the coordinate is the building centroid. OpenStreetMap is a rank-11 source, so the point is recorded as approximate; precision_m is the half-size of the footprint. Previous record: campus point 41.8422582, -88.245782 at 3000 m precision.

name: D0 collision hall (Tevatron D0)
notes: Coordinates reuse the sourced Fermilab main-campus point from site:fermilab-main-campus (src:fermilab-lbnf-dune-site), per the wave-3 brief's explicit fallback for a detector hall whose own coordinates are not separately published: a sourced campus point marked approximate. No source found this session gives a dedicated lat/lon for this specific interaction hall; the Tevatron ring (about 6.3 km circumference, about 1 km radius) means the true position could be up to roughly 2 km from this point.

fnal.gov states "DZero is one of two detectors positioned along the four-mile Tevatron accelerator ring. It takes its name from its location on the ring, D0." (src:colliders-historical-d0-fnal-tevatron-experiments-page), confirming the D0 location name, though not coordinates.

summary.plain: The interaction hall on the Fermilab Tevatron ring where the D0 detector sat, in Batavia, Illinois. Its own precise position is not published in a source found this session, so it is shown at the precision of the wider Fermilab site.
summary.technical: D0 collision hall (Tevatron D0): one of the Tevatron ring's interaction regions, at Fermilab, Batavia, Illinois. No dedicated survey coordinate for the hall itself was found; shown at Fermilab campus precision (~3 km) as an approximate marker.
